questions.question_stem: A learner says, "My bitcoin is inside my wallet app, so losing the app deletes the coins." Which correction is best?
questions.correct_answer: The coins are represented on-chain as UTXOs; the wallet manages keys, addresses, policies, and signatures that authorize spending them.
incorrect_answers: The coins are cached locally by the wallet app; the blockchain only records backup hints, labels, and recovery data for that wallet app.
The coins are tracked on-chain as account balances; the wallet signs balance updates that nodes apply to the user's account.
The coins are stored under one permanent receiving address; the wallet keeps the password that unlocks the address for spending.
questions.explanation: The lesson frames a wallet as a local key and policy manager, not as a coin container. Spendable value remains on-chain as UTXOs controlled by the relevant spending conditions.
questions.lesson_block: A wallet holds keys, not coins
questions.specific_source_lesson: 05-BF-wallet_types.qmd: A wallet holds keys, not coins / A wallet manages many keys and addresses

questions.question_stem: Why can one seed phrase often recover many receiving addresses in a Bitcoin wallet?
questions.correct_answer: The wallet can deterministically derive many private keys, public keys, and addresses from the seed phrase.
incorrect_answers: The seed phrase lists every receiving address, so the wallet reloads addresses directly from the words.
The wallet can ask full nodes to restore a master account balance that was registered on-chain to the seed phrase.
The seed phrase stores copies of wallet UTXOs, so recovery rebroadcasts those outputs to the network.
questions.explanation: A deterministic wallet can regenerate a family of keys and addresses from one backup root. The seed phrase restores spending authority; it does not recreate coins outside the blockchain.
questions.lesson_block: One seed grows a whole tree of keys
questions.specific_source_lesson: 05-BF-wallet_types.qmd: A seed phrase is the whole wallet as words / One seed grows a whole tree of keys
